powers_off_instead.what: The way back cannot delete tunl0, which the kernel keeps

warnings: The way back cannot delete tunl0, which the kernel keeps, so the machine powers off instead of returning to the decoy. `sudo /mnt/data/nails deactivate --poweroff` powers off at once.

The return cannot number the decoy's processes from where its own boot numbered them, so where the decoy keeps classic wtmp, its getty and login records carry process numbers that continue from this boot. `sudo /mnt/data/nails deactivate --poweroff` leaves none of them.
